items.title: Mrs. Francis Oliver Interview, 1969-05-10
items.q: Tony Jackson was dead at that time.

ctx.x: And I mean, the funny thing about it, you try to tell your people the truth, you know what I mean? And my grandmother said, well, you evasive. Something's wrong. You know something that you're not telling me. And here it all came out. I would tell everything.
Do you remember anybody else coming to the house that he played with? Any other musicians? I would have done. No. Tony Jackson was dead at that time.

But, Jelly, you listen here, he would come alone to pick me up. He'd come and visit me alone. He'd ever bring any of his friends around. And he would always, he'd give me some kind of excuse when I said, well, tomorrow we're going downtown, may I stop over there? And he said, no, baby, I'll let you know when you can come. And he always wanted to treat me like I was still 16, you know. You just couldn't imagine I was married and had a child. But I told him one time, I said, I'd never been to Dry Street until I got…
